# 3.3 · Honest Metrics

`Level 3: Classic ML, No Excuses` · `+20 XP` · `drill 3 of 3`

## The job
Write the scoreboard. `train_test_split(rows, test_frac, seed)` shuffles a copy with a
seeded `random.Random` and returns `(train, test)` with `round(len(rows) * test_frac)` rows
in test. `confusion` counts tp, fp, fn and tn. `accuracy` is the share of exact matches.
`precision_recall_f1` returns all three, using 0.0 whenever a ratio would divide by zero.

## Why it matters
A model that always says "not fraud" is 99 percent accurate when 1 percent of cases are
fraud, and completely useless. Precision and recall expose that. Seeded splits make
experiments repeatable, so a better number means a better model and not a luckier shuffle.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 3.3     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 3.3      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. `random.Random(seed).shuffle(copy)` keeps the caller's list intact and the order reproducible.
2. Precision asks "of everything I flagged, how much was right?" Recall asks "of everything I should have flagged, how much did I catch?"
3. F1 is the harmonic mean, 2PR / (P + R), and is 0.0 when P + R is 0.
4. Raise ValueError when y_true and y_pred have different lengths.

</details>
